```text
77	_aiagent_autodetect() {
78	  local cand
79	  # Word-split $AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY. The original `${=…}` was zsh's explicit

89	      printf '%s\n' "$cand"
90	      return 0
91	    fi
92	  done
93	  return 1
94	}

96	# Background spinner on stderr while the agent is thinking. Skipped when
97	# AICAP_SPINNER=0 or stderr isn't a tty (so pipes / file redirects stay
98	# clean). The spinner subprocess is disowned via `& disown` so it survives
99	# the command substitution that invokes the agent.
100	_AICAP_SPIN_PID=
101	_aicap_spinner_start() {
102	  [ "$AICAP_SPINNER" != "1" ] && return 0
103	  [ ! -t 2 ] && return 0
104	  local label="${1:-thinking}"
105	  (
106	    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT HUP

108	    frames=('⠋' '⠙' '⠹' '⠸' '⠼' '⠴' '⠦' '⠧' '⠇' '⠏')

113	      printf '\r\e[K%s %s' "${frames[*]:$(( i % 10 )):1}" "$label" >&2
114	      i=$(( i + 1 ))
115	      sleep 0.1
116	    done
117	  ) & disown

119	}

126	  _AICAP_SPIN_PID=

144	# Invoke a coding-agent in one-shot mode.

146	# Writes reply (text) to stdout. Writes metadata line to stderr when
147	# AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1 and the agent supports structured JSON output.
148	# Currently only Claude's JSON includes usage/cost — other agents just get a
149	# "<agent> (<model>)" line on stderr.
150	_aiagent_invoke() {
151	  local agent="$1" prompt="$2"
152	  local json reply model_used tokens_in tokens_out cache_read cache_create cost duration rc
153	
154	  # Ensure spinner cleans up if the caller returns or we hit a trap.
155	  trap '_aicap_spinner_stop' EXIT INT TERM

157	  case "$agent" in
158	    claude)
159	      # Conditional --model: empty AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL → claude picks its

161	      local -a claude_model_args
162	      claude_model_args=()
163	      [ -n "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL" ] && claude_model_args=(--model "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL")

165	      if [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" = "1" ] && command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
166	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $claude_model_label (json)…"
167	        json=$(claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" --output-format json "$prompt")
168	        rc=$?
169	        _aicap_spinner_stop
170	        (( rc != 0 )) && return $rc
171	        reply=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.result // empty')
172	        model_used=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.modelUsage | keys | first // "?"')
173	        tokens_in=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.input_tokens // "?"')
174	        tokens_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.output_tokens // "?"')
175	        cache_read=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_read_input_tokens // 0')
176	        cache_create=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens // 0')
177	        cost=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.total_cost_usd // "?"')
178	        duration=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.duration_ms // "?"')
179	        printf '%s\n' "claude ($model_used) | in=$tokens_in out=$tokens_out cache=(r:$cache_read,w:$cache_create) | cost=\$$cost ${duration}ms" >&2
180	        printf '%s\n' "$reply"
181	      else
182	        printf '%s\n' "claude ($claude_model_label)" >&2
183	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $claude_model_label…"
184	        claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
185	        rc=$?
186	        _aicap_spinner_stop
187	        return $rc
188	      fi
189	      ;;
190	    opencode)
191	      local -a opencode_model_args
192	      opencode_model_args=()
193	      [ -n "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL" ] && opencode_model_args=(-m "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL")
194	      local opencode_model_label="${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL:-(default)}"
195	      printf '%s\n' "opencode ($opencode_model_label)" >&2
196	      _aicap_spinner_start "opencode $opencode_model_label…"
197	      opencode run "${opencode_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
198	      rc=$?
199	      _aicap_spinner_stop
200	      return $rc
201	      ;;
202	    codex)
203	      # AICAP_CODEX_MODEL defaults to empty since gpt-5-mini is rejected on
204	      # ChatGPT-account auth. Users on API-key auth can re-pin via the env.
205	      local -a codex_model_args
206	      codex_model_args=()
207	      [ -n "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL" ] && codex_model_args=(-m "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL")
208	      local codex_model_label="${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL:-(default)}"
209	      printf '%s\n' "codex ($codex_model_label)" >&2
210	      _aicap_spinner_start "codex $codex_model_label…"
211	      codex exec "${codex_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
212	      rc=$?
213	      _aicap_spinner_stop
214	      return $rc
215	      ;;
216	    cursor-agent)
217	      if [ -n "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" ]; then
218	        printf '%s\n' "cursor-agent ($AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL)" >&2
219	        _aicap_spinner_start "cursor-agent $AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL…"
220	        cursor-agent -p --model "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" "$prompt"
221	      else
222	        printf '%s\n' "cursor-agent" >&2
223	        _aicap_spinner_start "cursor-agent…"
224	        cursor-agent -p "$prompt"
225	      fi
226	      rc=$?
227	      _aicap_spinner_stop
228	      return $rc
229	      ;;
230	    http)
231	      # OpenAI-compatible chat-completions over curl. Covers OpenRouter (with
232	      # API key) and local Ollama (no auth) with the same code path. Never
233	      # auto-detected — opt in via AICAP_AGENT=http or `-a http`.
234	      local url="$AICAP_HTTP_URL" model="$AICAP_HTTP_MODEL"
235	      local key="${AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:-${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}}"
236	      if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
237	        printf '%s\n' "aifix: jq is required for the http agent" >&2
238	        return 1
239	      fi
240	      if ! command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
241	        printf '%s\n' "aifix: curl is required for the http agent" >&2
242	        return 1
243	      fi
244	      # Extract host from URL. Original used zsh-nested `${${url#*://}%%/*}`;
245	      # bash doesn't support nested expansion, so do it in two steps.
246	      local host
247	      host="${url#*://}"
248	      host="${host%%/*}"
249	      [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" != "1" ] && printf '%s\n' "http ($model @ $host)" >&2
250	      _aicap_spinner_start "http $model…"
251	      local payload response
252	      payload=$(jq -n --arg m "$model" --arg p "$prompt" \
253	        '{model: $m, messages: [{role: "user", content: $p}], stream: false}')
254	      local -a curl_args
255	      curl_args=(-sS -X POST "$url" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$payload")
256	      [ -n "$key" ] && curl_args+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $key")
257	      response=$(curl "${curl_args[@]}")
258	      rc=$?
259	      _aicap_spinner_stop
260	      if (( rc != 0 )); then
261	        printf '%s\n' "http: curl failed (rc=$rc) — check AICAP_HTTP_URL ($url)" >&2
262	        return $rc
263	      fi
264	      local err
265	      err=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.error.message // (.error | strings) // empty' 2>/dev/null)
266	      if [ -n "$err" ]; then
267	        printf '%s\n' "http: API error: $err" >&2
268	        return 1
269	      fi
270	      reply=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.choices[0].message.content // empty')
271	      if [ -z "$reply" ]; then
272	        printf '%s\n' "http: empty reply (raw response: $response)" >&2
273	        return 1
274	      fi
275	      if [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" = "1" ]; then
276	        tokens_in=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.usage.prompt_tokens // "?"')
277	        tokens_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.usage.completion_tokens // "?"')
278	        printf '%s\n' "http ($model @ $host) | in=$tokens_in out=$tokens_out" >&2
279	      fi
280	      printf '%s\n' "$reply"
281	      ;;
282	    *) printf '%s\n' "aifix: unknown agent '$agent' (supported: opencode, claude, codex, cursor-agent, http)" >&2; return 1 ;;
283	  esac
284	}

286	# Core dispatcher: given an already-captured block, build the prompt, invoke
287	# the agent, pipe reply through the prettifier. Shared by the four sources:
288	# cpblock (aifix/aiexplain), stdin (aifix-stdin), tee'd CMD run (aifix-run),
289	# and thefuck-style rerun (aifix-rerun).
290	#
291	#   _ai_dispatch_core <name> <source-label> <default-prompt>
292	#                     <agent> <raw> <no-meta> <prompt-override> <block>
293	_ai_dispatch_core() {
294	  local name="$1" source_label="$2" default_prompt="$3"
295	  local agent="$4" raw="$5" no_meta="$6" prompt_override="$7" block="$8"
296	  if [ -z "$block" ]; then
297	    printf '%s\n' "$name: empty block" >&2
298	    return 1
299	  fi
300	  local prompt="${prompt_override:-$default_prompt}
301	
302	$block"
303	  printf '%s\n' "$name ← $source_label" >&2
304	
305	  # Per-call env overrides: --no-meta / --raw flip env-var behaviour locally
306	  # so _aiagent_invoke + _aicap_prettify see the intended values.
307	  local saved_show="$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" saved_pretty="$AICAP_PRETTIFY"
308	  (( no_meta )) && AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=0
309	  (( raw ))    && AICAP_PRETTIFY=0
310	
311	  if (( raw )); then
312	    _aiagent_invoke "$agent" "$prompt"
313	  else
314	    _aiagent_invoke "$agent" "$prompt" | _aicap_prettify
315	  fi
316	  local rc=$?
317	
318	  AICAP_SHOW_METADATA="$saved_show"
319	  AICAP_PRETTIFY="$saved_pretty"
320	  return $rc
321	}
322	
323	# Print the shared flag-help + env-var snapshot. Used by -h on each wrapper.
324	_ai_print_help() {
325	  local name="$1" usage="$2"
326	  printf '%s\n' "usage: $name $usage"
327	  printf '%s\n' "  -a AGENT   claude | opencode | codex | cursor-agent | http (default: auto-detect)"
328	  printf '%s\n' "  -p PROMPT  override default prompt"
329	  printf '%s\n' "  --raw      disable prettify (glow/bat), print raw agent reply"
330	  printf '%s\n' "  --no-meta  suppress the stderr metadata line"
331	  printf '%s\n' ""
332	  printf '%s\n' "env vars:"
333	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_AGENT          = ${AICAP_AGENT:-<unset = auto-detect>}"
334	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL}"
335	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL = ${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL}"
336	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_CODEX_MODEL    = ${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL}"
337	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL:-<unset>}"
338	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_HTTP_URL       = ${AICAP_HTTP_URL}"
339	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_HTTP_MODEL     = ${AICAP_HTTP_MODEL}"
340	  if [ -n "${AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:-${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}}" ]; then
341	    printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY   = <set>"
342	  else
343	    printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY   = <unset>"
344	  fi
345	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_SHOW_METADATA  = ${AICAP_SHOW_METADATA}"
346	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_PRETTIFY       = ${AICAP_PRETTIFY}"
347	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_SPINNER        = ${AICAP_SPINNER}"
348	}

350	# Shared dispatcher for aifix / aiexplain. Captures via cpblock (zsh-only).
351	_ai_capture_dispatch() {
352	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
353	  local name="$1"; shift
354	  local default_prompt="$1"; shift
355	  local n=1 agent="" prompt_override="" raw=0 no_meta=0
356	  while (( $# )); do
357	    case "$1" in
358	      -a|--agent)   agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
359	      -p|--prompt)  prompt_override="$2"; shift 2 ;;
360	      --raw)        raw=1; shift ;;
361	      --no-meta)    no_meta=1; shift ;;
362	      -h|--help)    _ai_print_help "$name" "[N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]"
363	                    printf '%s\n' "  N          block index back (default 1 = last)"
364	                    return 0 ;;
365	      --) shift; break ;;
366	      -*) printf '%s\n' "$name: unknown flag: $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
367	      *)  n="$1"; shift ;;
368	    esac
369	  done
370	  if ! [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
371	    printf '%s\n' "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n)" >&2
372	    return 1
373	  fi
374	  if [ -z "$agent" ]; then
375	    if [ -n "$AICAP_AGENT" ]; then
376	      agent="$AICAP_AGENT"
377	    else
378	      agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
379	        printf '%s\n' "$name: no coding-agent CLI found on PATH (tried: opencode, claude, codex, cursor-agent)" >&2
380	        printf '%s\n' "$name: hint — set AICAP_AGENT=http to use OpenRouter / Ollama directly" >&2
381	        return 1
382	      }
383	    fi
384	  fi
385	  if ! command -v cpblock &>/dev/null; then
386	    printf '%s\n' "$name: cpblock not defined (zsh-only; loaded from dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh)" >&2
387	    printf '%s\n' "$name: in bash, use \`aifix-stdin\` / \`aifix-run\` / \`aifix-rerun\` instead" >&2
388	    return 1
389	  fi
390	  local block
391	  block=$(cpblock "$n" 2>/dev/null) || {
392	    printf '%s\n' "$name: cpblock $n failed (run 'exec zsh' if the shell pre-dates chezmoi apply)" >&2
393	    return 1
394	  }
395	  _ai_dispatch_core "$name" "block -$n" "$default_prompt" \
396	    "$agent" "$raw" "$no_meta" "$prompt_override" "$block"
397	}
```

```text
1	# Custom Aliases & Shell Functions
2	
3	Quick reference for custom aliases and shell functions defined in this dotfiles repo. Available in zsh, bash, or both — the source file path tells you which:
4	
5	- `dot_config/shell/*.sh` — POSIX layer, sourced by **both** `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`.
6	- `dot_config/zsh/*.zsh` (or `tools/*.zsh`) — **zsh-only**.
7	- `dot_config/bash/*.bash` — **bash-only**.
8	
9	> **Maintenance rule** (mirrored in `CLAUDE.md`): whenever you add, modify, or remove a custom alias or shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/`, update this table — include the type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description. Place new helpers in the right tier per the [CLAUDE.md three-tier rule](../../CLAUDE.md#custom-aliases--shell-functions--docsshellsaliasesmd).

461	| `sesh-here` / `shere` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Lightweight: bare shell session at `$PWD` (no nvim, no project layout). Pass args/`-c CMD` to override |
462	| `sesh-root` / `sroot` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Connect sesh to current git root (falls back to `$PWD`); honors sesh.toml wildcards/default |
463	| `sesh-code` / `scode` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Repo-scoped coding-agent layout: nvim 75% \| `specstory run [agent]` 25%, plus btop window. Session named `coding-agent/<repo>` (collision-safe). Refuses outside git repos. Flags: `--on-exit shell\|kill\|restart`, `--no-specstory` |

N tiled agent panes + lazygit window + nvim window. Session named `vibe/<repo>`. Same `--on-exit` / `--no-specstory` flags as scode. Requires bash 4+ when invoked from bash |

Default `--on-exit shell` keeps the session alive after CMD exits (drops to login shell, re-run via history-Up); `-k` restores fire-and-forget kill semantics. 546	### Proxy helpers
547	
548	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs); otherwise prefers an active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:` from `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` or `~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml`) before falling back to probing ports 7890/7891/1087/8118/8080 with `nc -z -w1`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache before the next lookup. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block.
549	
550	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
551	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
552	| `withproxy` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Run a single command with proxy env vars exported to the child only (e.g. `withproxy curl ...`) |
553	| `try_direct_then_proxy` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Run a command direct; on failure, retry via `withproxy`. Used as the default for reader functions. |
554	| `proxy-on` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Export `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` in the current shell |
555	| `proxy-off` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Unset all proxy env vars in the current shell |
556	| `proxy-status` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Report state: **active** (exported), **available** (detected), or **unavailable** |
557	| `proxy-test` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Test detected proxy egress with `curl https://www.google.com/generate_204` (HTTP, not ICMP ping) |
558	| `proxy-refresh` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Clear cached detection, re-probe, print status (use after toggling your proxy) |
559	
560	### Web reader
561	
562	> Render web pages as markdown in the terminal. All functions use `try_direct_then_proxy` so non-GFW'd URLs pay zero proxy overhead. Pick the extractor by function name. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md).

564	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
565	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|

567	| `readlocal` | function | `dot_config/shell/55_web_reader.sh` | Read article via trafilatura + glow (local, offline) *(requires `trafilatura`)* |
568	| `readnode` | function | `dot_config/shell/55_web_reader.sh` | Read article via readability-cli (`readable`) + glow (Mozilla Readability) *(requires `readable`)* |
569	| `readraw` | function | `dot_config/shell/55_web_reader.sh` | Render full page: `curl | pandoc -f html -t gfm | glow -` (no article extraction) *(requires `pandoc`)* |

626	## macOS apps
627	
628	> Graceful GUI app control via `osascript` + Apple Events. Prefer over `killall` for apps with state (OrbStack, Docker Desktop, Slack, etc.) — `quit` sends ⌘Q-equivalent, letting the app tear down cleanly. App NAME is the AppleScript name (e.g. `OrbStack`, `Google Chrome`), not bundle ID; passed via `osascript argv` so spaces/quotes are safe.
629	
630	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
631	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
632	| `appquit <AppName>` | function | `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` (macOS), `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` (Linux) | **Cross-platform.** macOS: Quit Apple Event (graceful, equivalent to ⌘Q). Linux: `pkill -TERM -f <pattern>` resolved from `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` overrides or auto-derived from `.desktop` scan; Electron + Firefox honour SIGTERM as graceful quit. |
633	| `applaunch <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** macOS: launch in background (no focus steal). Linux: `gtk-launch <desktop-id>` via `setsid -f`. App-defined startup behaviour applies. |
634	| `appactivate <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** macOS: launch + bring to front. Linux: D-Bus call to GNOME `window-calls` extension if installed (best fidelity), otherwise falls back to `applaunch` (single-instance apps re-focus). |
635	| `apprestart <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** `appquit` + poll until process gone (≤15s) + `applaunch`. On Linux, launches the app even if it wasn't running (mirrors macOS silent-quit semantics). |
636	| `apprunning <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** Silent predicate; exit 0 if running, 1 otherwise. Linux backend: `pgrep -f <pattern>`. |
637	| `applist [--pids\|--all]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** Default: names of running apps the helper recognises. `--pids` adds `<pid>\t<name>` (used by `tv {mac,linux}-apps`). macOS lists foreground GUI apps via System Events; Linux enumerates registered overrides + auto-derived from `.desktop` scan filtered to running processes. Linux `--all` shows non-running entries too. |
638	| `appresponsive <AppName> [TIMEOUT_SEC]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, divergent fidelity.** macOS: best-effort "Not Responding" via timed-out Apple Event. Linux: only meaningful for apps registered with `--mpris=NAME` (Spotify, mpv, VLC); for Electron/Firefox/most apps it degrades to `apprunning` with a stderr note — no public Linux API analog to macOS Apple Events. |
639	| `linux_app_register NAME [OPTS]` | function | `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` | **Linux-only.** Register an app for the Linux `app-*` helpers — `--desktop=ID --pkill=REGEX --wm-class=CLASS [--mpris=NAME]`. Typical call site: `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` (sourced at shell startup, never auto-stubbed). Override file matters for AppImage / Snap / Flatpak where auto-derivation can't resolve the runtime binary path — see `pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md`. `linux_app_register --list` prints the current registry. |

Reuses the AI Capture agent fallback (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent); 10-min cached in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/`. `-d` includes the visible area of each session's active pane (20-100 lines, self-capture skipped); set `TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1` in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` to make `-d` implicit (override with `--shallow`). `--sort closability` orders keep → check → safe (default: alphabetical); `--only {safe,check,keep}` filters to one tier. `-r` bypasses cache; `-i` opens fzf picker that switches client on Enter (also reachable via tmux `prefix + Space → Sessions → AI session summary`); `--dry-run` prints the prompt without calling the LLM. **On hosts with multiple tmux binaries** (apt + appimage, brew + system) export `TSUM_TMUX_BIN=/path/to/tmux` so tsum talks to the right server. |

696	> One-shot pipeline: capture a past block (via `cpblock N`) and pass it to a coding-agent CLI (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent) in non-interactive / advisory mode. 5	# that walks SQLite + JSONL + store.db and emits a single TSV stream).
```
```text
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   tv agent-sessions
9	#
10	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
11	#   1. All agents merged       (default — globally sorted DESC by mtime)
12	#   2. OpenCode only           (~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db)
13	#   3. Claude Code only        (~/.claude/projects/**/<sid>.jsonl)
14	#   4. Codex only              (~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl)
15	#   5. Cursor Agent CLI only   (~/.cursor/chats/<wsHash>/<chatId>/store.db)
16	#   6. Cursor IDE composers    (~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/{globalStorage,workspaceStorage})
17	#
18	# Agent tags: [oc] OpenCode, [cc] Claude Code, [cx] Codex,
19	#             [cu] Cursor Agent CLI, [ci] Cursor IDE composer chats
20	#
21	# Title/snippet column is the first non-system user message (truncated 140ch),
22	# so TV's fuzzy search matches by content as well as date / project / id.
23	#
24	# Each row also carries a matched `.specstory/history/*.md` path (col 5) when
25	# SpecStory has written one for that session — see docs/tools/specstory-internals.md.
26	#
27	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
28	#   1. Metadata header + full chat transcript (glow-rendered; prefers the
29	#      .specstory/history/*.md file when present, falls back to raw-source
30	#      walk for live sessions). Cursor [cu]/[ci] show a "deferred" note and
31	#      the legacy first-5 view in cycle 2 instead — see the backlog entry
32	#      backlog/tv-agent-sessions-richer-preview.md.
33	#   2. Metadata header + first 5 user messages (legacy; kept for fast
34	#      content search across sessions).
35	#   3. Raw record dump (head 200 lines / SQL dump).
36	#
37	# Keybindings:
38	#   Enter      Print resume one-liner to stdout (cd <dir> && <agent-cmd> <id>)
39	#   Alt+T      Resume in same shell (cd + exec; T for "take over")
40	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy session ID to clipboard
41	#   Alt+P      Copy directory path to clipboard
42	#   Alt+R      Copy resume one-liner to clipboard
43	#   Alt+S      Copy matched .specstory/history/*.md path to clipboard (S for SpecStory)
44	#   Alt+E      Open raw session file in $EDITOR (claude/codex only)
45	#
46	# Ctrl+E is left as TV's global `go_to_input_end`.
47	
48	[metadata]
49	name = "agent-sessions"
50	description = "Coding-agent sessions: OpenCode + Claude Code + Codex + Cursor (CLI & IDE) — content-searchable"
51	requirements = ["python3", "bat"]
52	
53	[source]
54	# Each cycle calls the helper with a different mode. Mode "all" is the default.
55	# TSV columns produced by the helper:
56	#   0. agent  ([oc]/[cc]/[cx]/[cu])
57	#   1. when   (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM)
58	#   2. id     (session id)
59	#   3. dir    (cwd)
60	#   4. title/snippet
61	command = [
62	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py all",
63	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py opencode",
64	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py claude",
65	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py codex",
66	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py cursor",
67	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py cursor-ide",
68	]
69	display = "{split:\t:0} {split:\t:1}  │  {split:\t:4}  │  {split:\t:3|split:/:-1}"
70	output = "{split:\t:2}"
71	
72	[preview]
73	command = [
74	  # Preview 1 (default): metadata header + full chat transcript.
75	  #
76	  # The transcript is rendered by the Python helper's `transcript` mode,
77	  # which prefers the matched .specstory/history/*.md file (col 5) when
78	  # present and falls back to walking the raw session source for live
79	  # sessions. Output is piped through `glow` (if installed) or `bat`.
80	  #
81	  # IMPORTANT: do NOT embed Python/awk/JSON literals inline here — any bare
82	  # `{...}` in this string (outside TV's own `{split:...}`/`{strip_ansi}`
83	  # placeholders) silently breaks ALL placeholder substitution in the same
84	  # command. See pitfalls/tv-channel-bare-braces-break-substitution.md.
85	  # Keep the rich logic in the helper; this block is just shell glue.
86	  '''
87	  agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'; when='{split:\t:1}'; ss='{split:\t:5}'
88	  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$sid" "$when"
89	  printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m       %s\n' "$dir"
90	  if [ -n "$ss" ]; then
91	    printf '\033[2mspecstory:\033[0m %s\n' "$ss"
92	  fi
93	  case "$agent" in
94	    "[oc]")
95	      sqlite3 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" \
96	        "SELECT 'title=    ' || title || char(10) || 'version=  ' || version FROM session WHERE id = '$sid';" 2>/dev/null
97	      ;;
98	    "[cc]")
99	      f=$(find "$HOME/.claude/projects" -name "${sid}.jsonl" -not -path "*/subagents/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
100	      [ -n "$f" ] && printf 'file:      %s\n' "$f"
101	      ;;
102	    "[cx]")
103	      f=$(find "$HOME/.codex/sessions" -name "rollout-*${sid}*.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
104	      [ -n "$f" ] && printf 'file:      %s\n' "$f"
105	      ;;
106	  esac
107	  printf '\n'
108	  case "$agent" in
109	    "[cc]") tag=cc ;;
110	    "[cx]") tag=cx ;;
111	    "[oc]") tag=oc ;;
112	    *) tag="" ;;
113	  esac
114	  if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
115	    printf '\033[2m(transcript rendering deferred for %s — press Ctrl+F to cycle to the legacy first-5 view.)\033[0m\n' "$agent"
116	    exit 0
117	  fi
118	  if command -v glow >/dev/null 2>&1; then
119	    "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null \
120	      | glow --style auto - 2>/dev/null \
121	      || "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null
122	  else
123	    "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null \
124	      | bat -l md --color=always --plain --paging=never 2>/dev/null \
125	      || "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null
126	  fi
127	  ''',
128	  # Preview 2 (legacy): metadata + first 5 user messages — kept because
129	  # content-searching sessions by "did I talk about X?" is faster here
130	  # than scrolling a full transcript.
131	  '''
132	  agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'; when='{split:\t:1}'
133	  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$sid" "$when"
134	  printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n\n' "$dir"
135	  case "$agent" in
136	    "[oc]")
137	      sqlite3 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" \
138	        "SELECT 'title=' || title || char(10) || 'version=' || version || char(10) || 'project_id=' || project_id || char(10) || coalesce('share=' || share_url, '') FROM session WHERE id = '$sid';" 2>/dev/null
139	      printf '\n\033[1mFirst 5 user messages:\033[0m\n'
140	      sqlite3 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" "
141	        SELECT '  ' || substr(replace(replace(json_extract(p.data, '\$.text'), char(10), ' '), '  ', ' '), 1, 280)
142	        FROM part p JOIN message m ON p.message_id = m.id
143	        WHERE p.session_id = '$sid'
144	          AND m.data LIKE '%\"role\":\"user\"%'
145	          AND p.data LIKE '%\"type\":\"text\"%'
146	          AND p.data NOT LIKE '%\"synthetic\":true%'
147	        ORDER BY p.time_created ASC
148	        LIMIT 5;" 2>/dev/null
149	      ;;
150	    "[cc]")
151	      f=$(find "$HOME/.claude/projects" -name "${sid}.jsonl" -not -path "*/subagents/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
152	      if [ -n "$f" ]; then
153	        printf 'file: %s\n\n' "$f"
154	        printf '\033[1mFirst 5 user messages:\033[0m\n'
155	        head -200 "$f" | python3 -c "
156	import sys, json, re
157	n=0
158	for line in sys.stdin:
159	  try: d=json.loads(line)
160	  except: continue
161	  if d.get('type') != 'user': continue
162	  m=d.get('message') or dict()
163	  c=m.get('content')
164	  txt=''
165	  if isinstance(c,str): txt=c
166	  elif isinstance(c,list):
167	    for p in c:
168	      if isinstance(p,dict) and p.get('type')=='text': txt=p.get('text',''); break
169	  if not txt or txt.lstrip().startswith(('<','#')): continue
170	  txt=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',txt).strip()[:300]
171	  print('  ' + txt)
172	  n+=1
173	  if n>=5: break
174	" 2>/dev/null
175	      else
176	        echo "(jsonl not found for $sid)"
177	      fi
178	      ;;
179	    "[cx]")
180	      f=$(find "$HOME/.codex/sessions" -name "rollout-*${sid}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
181	      if [ -n "$f" ]; then
182	        printf 'file: %s\n\n' "$f"
183	        printf '\033[1mFirst 5 user messages:\033[0m\n'
184	        head -200 "$f" | python3 -c "
185	import sys, json, re
186	n=0
187	for line in sys.stdin:
188	  try: d=json.loads(line)
189	  except: continue
190	  if d.get('type')!='response_item': continue
191	  p=d.get('payload') or dict()
192	  if p.get('type')!='message' or p.get('role')!='user': continue
193	  for c in p.get('content',[]):
194	    if isinstance(c,dict) and c.get('type') in ('input_text','text'):
195	      txt=c.get('text','')
196	      if not txt or txt.lstrip().startswith('<'): continue
197	      txt=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',txt).strip()[:300]
198	      print('  ' + txt)
199	      n+=1
200	      break
201	  if n>=5: break
202	" 2>/dev/null
203	      else
204	        echo "(rollout not found for $sid)"
205	      fi
206	      ;;
207	    "[cu]")
208	      db=$(find "$HOME/.cursor/chats" -path "*/${sid}/store.db" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
209	      if [ -n "$db" ]; then
210	        printf 'db: %s\n\n' "$db"
211	        # meta value is hex-encoded JSON; decode and pretty-print
212	        sqlite3 "$db" "SELECT value FROM meta LIMIT 1;" 2>/dev/null \
213	          | python3 -c "
214	import sys, json
215	raw = sys.stdin.read().strip()
216	try: text = bytes.fromhex(raw).decode('utf-8','replace')
217	except ValueError: text = raw
218	try:
219	    d = json.loads(text)
220	    for k in ('name','mode','lastUsedModel','agentId','createdAt','latestRootBlobId'):
221	        if k in d:
222	            v = d[k]
223	            print('  ' + k + ': ' + str(v))
224	except Exception:
225	    print(text[:500])
226	" 2>/dev/null
227	        printf '\n\033[1mFirst 5 user messages:\033[0m\n'
228	        # Read blobs directly via python sqlite3 (avoids CLI binary/newline issues)
229	        python3 -c "
230	import sqlite3, json, re, sys
231	con = sqlite3.connect('file:$db?mode=ro', uri=True)
232	n = 0
233	for (data,) in con.execute('SELECT data FROM blobs'):
234	  if isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
235	    try: text = bytes(data).decode('utf-8','replace')
236	    except Exception: continue
237	  else:
238	    text = str(data)
239	  try: d = json.loads(text)
240	  except Exception: continue
241	  if not isinstance(d, dict): continue
242	  if d.get('role') != 'user': continue
243	  c = d.get('content')
244	  txt = ''
245	  if isinstance(c, str): txt = c
246	  elif isinstance(c, list):
247	    for p in c:
248	      if isinstance(p, dict) and p.get('type') == 'text':
249	        txt = p.get('text',''); break
250	  if not txt: continue
251	  s = txt.lstrip()
252	  if s.startswith(('<user_info>','<system_reminder>','<attached_files>','<environment_context>','<local-command-','<system-reminder>','# AGENTS','Caveat:')):
253	    continue
254	  txt = re.sub(r'\s+',' ', txt).strip()[:280]
255	  print('  ' + txt)
256	  n += 1
257	  if n >= 5: break
258	con.close()
259	if n == 0:
260	  print('  (no user-role blobs found; chat may use a different schema)')
261	" 2>/dev/null
262	        printf '\n'
263	        sqlite3 "$db" "SELECT count(*) || ' blob(s)' FROM blobs;" 2>/dev/null
264	      else
265	        echo "(store.db not found for $sid)"
266	      fi
267	      ;;
268	    "[ci]")
269	      gdb="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb"
270	      [ -f "$gdb" ] || gdb="$HOME/.config/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb"
271	      if [ ! -f "$gdb" ]; then
272	        echo "(Cursor IDE state.vscdb not found)"
273	      else
274	        printf 'db: %s\n\n' "$gdb"
275	        # Composer metadata
276	        sqlite3 "$gdb" "SELECT value FROM cursorDiskKV WHERE key='composerData:$sid';" 2>/dev/null \
277	          | python3 -c "
278	import sys, json
279	raw = sys.stdin.read().strip()
280	if not raw:
281	  print('  (composer not found)')
282	else:
283	  try:
284	    d = json.loads(raw)
285	    for k in ('name','subtitle','unifiedMode','forceMode','status','contextUsagePercent'):
286	      if k in d and d[k] not in (None, ''):
287	        print('  ' + k + ': ' + str(d[k])[:200])
288	    heads = d.get('fullConversationHeadersOnly') or list()
289	    print('  bubbles: ' + str(len(heads)) + ' (user: ' + str(sum(1 for h in heads if h.get('type')==1)) + ', assistant: ' + str(sum(1 for h in heads if h.get('type')==2)) + ')')
290	  except Exception as e:
291	    print('  (parse error: ' + str(e) + ')')
292	" 2>/dev/null
293	        printf '\n\033[1mFirst 5 user messages:\033[0m\n'
294	        python3 -c "
295	import sqlite3, json, re
296	con = sqlite3.connect('file:$gdb?mode=ro', uri=True)
297	row = con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM cursorDiskKV WHERE key='composerData:$sid'\").fetchone()
298	if not row or not row[0]:
299	  print('  (composer not found)')
300	else:
301	  d = json.loads(row[0])
302	  heads = d.get('fullConversationHeadersOnly') or list()
303	  n = 0
304	  for h in heads:
305	    if h.get('type') != 1: continue
306	    bid = h.get('bubbleId')
307	    if not bid: continue
308	    brow = con.execute('SELECT value FROM cursorDiskKV WHERE key = ?', ('bubbleId:$sid:' + bid,)).fetchone()
309	    if not brow or not brow[0]: continue
310	    try: bd = json.loads(brow[0])
311	    except Exception: continue
312	    txt = bd.get('text') or ''
313	    if not txt: continue
314	    s = txt.lstrip()
315	    if s.startswith(('<user_info>','<system_reminder>','<attached_files>','<environment_context>','<local-command-','<system-reminder>','# AGENTS','Caveat:')):
316	      continue
317	    txt = re.sub(r'\s+',' ', txt).strip()[:280]
318	    print('  ' + txt)
319	    n += 1
320	    if n >= 5: break
321	  if n == 0:
322	    print('  (no user-role bubbles found)')
323	con.close()
324	" 2>/dev/null
325	      fi
326	      ;;
327	  esac
328	  ''',
329	  # Preview 2: raw record dump.
330	  '''
331	  agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'
332	  case "$agent" in
333	    "[oc]")
334	      sqlite3 -header -column "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" \
335	        "SELECT id, title, directory, version, datetime(time_created/1000,'unixepoch','localtime') AS created FROM session WHERE id='$sid';" 2>/dev/null
336	      ;;
337	    "[cc]")
338	      f=$(find "$HOME/.claude/projects" -name "${sid}.jsonl" -not -path "*/subagents/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
339	      [ -n "$f" ] && head -200 "$f" | bat --color=always -l json --plain --paging=never 2>/dev/null \
340	        || [ -n "$f" ] && head -200 "$f" \
341	        || echo "(jsonl not found)"
342	      ;;
343	    "[cx]")
344	      f=$(find "$HOME/.codex/sessions" -name "rollout-*${sid}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
345	      [ -n "$f" ] && head -200 "$f" | bat --color=always -l json --plain --paging=never 2>/dev/null \
346	        || [ -n "$f" ] && head -200 "$f" \
347	        || echo "(rollout not found)"
348	      ;;
349	    "[cu]")
350	      db=$(find "$HOME/.cursor/chats" -path "*/${sid}/store.db" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
351	      [ -n "$db" ] && sqlite3 "$db" ".schema" 2>/dev/null
352	      ;;
353	    "[ci]")
354	      gdb="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb"
355	      [ -f "$gdb" ] || gdb="$HOME/.config/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb"
356	      [ -f "$gdb" ] && sqlite3 "$gdb" "SELECT value FROM cursorDiskKV WHERE key='composerData:$sid';" 2>/dev/null \
357	        | python3 -m json.tool 2>/dev/null | bat --color=always -l json --plain --paging=never 2>/dev/null \
358	        || echo "(composer not found)"
359	      ;;
360	  esac
361	  ''',
362	]
363	header = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:2}  ({split:\t:3})"
364	
365	[ui]
366	input_header = "Agent Sessions"
367	
368	[ui.preview_panel]
369	size = 60
370	
371	[keybindings]
372	enter = "actions:print_resume"
373	alt-t = "actions:resume"
374	ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
375	alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"
376	alt-r = "actions:copy_resume"
377	alt-s = "actions:copy_specstory"
378	alt-e = "actions:edit_jsonl"
379	
380	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
381	# Helper: assemble the agent-specific resume invocation.
382	# Each action sources `_resume_cmd` to keep the per-agent mapping in one place.
383	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
384	[actions.print_resume]
385	description = "Print 'cd <dir> && <agent> --resume <id>' to stdout"
386	command = '''
387	agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'
388	case "$agent" in
389	  "[oc]") cmd="opencode --session $sid" ;;
390	  "[cc]") cmd="claude --resume $sid" ;;
391	  "[cx]") cmd="codex resume $sid" ;;
392	  "[cu]") cmd="cursor-agent --resume $sid" ;;
393	  "[ci]") cmd="cursor   # IDE composer $sid (open from sidebar)" ;;
394	esac
395	case "$dir" in
396	  /*) printf 'cd %q && %s\n' "$dir" "$cmd" ;;
397	  vscode-remote://*) printf '%s   # remote: %s\n' "$cmd" "$dir" ;;
398	  *)  printf '%s   # cwd: %s\n' "$cmd" "$dir" ;;
399	esac
400	'''
401	mode = "execute"
402	
403	[actions.resume]
404	description = "cd to session dir and resume agent (in current terminal)"
405	command = '''
406	agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'
407	case "$dir" in /*) cd "$dir" 2>/dev/null || { echo "cd failed: $dir"; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 1; } ;; esac
408	case "$agent" in
409	  "[oc]") exec opencode --session "$sid" ;;
410	  "[cc]") exec claude --resume "$sid" ;;
411	  "[cx]") exec codex resume "$sid" ;;
412	  "[cu]") exec cursor-agent --resume "$sid" ;;
413	  "[ci]")
414	    case "$dir" in
415	      /*) exec cursor "$dir" ;;
416	      vscode-remote://*) echo "Remote workspace: $dir"; echo "Composer ID: $sid"; echo "Open Cursor and pick this chat from the sidebar."; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
417	      *) echo "Unknown workspace: $dir"; echo "Composer ID: $sid"; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
418	    esac
419	    ;;
420	esac
421	'''
422	mode = "execute"
423	
424	[actions.copy_id]
425	description = "Copy session ID to clipboard"
426	command = '''
427	d='{split:\t:2}'
428	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
429	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
430	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
431	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
432	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
433	fi
434	'''
435	mode = "fork"
436	
437	[actions.copy_dir]
438	description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
439	command = '''
440	d='{split:\t:3}'
441	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
442	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
443	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
444	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
445	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
446	fi
447	'''
448	mode = "fork"
449	
450	[actions.copy_specstory]
451	description = "Copy .specstory/history/*.md path to clipboard (SpecStory reverse-lookup)"
452	command = '''
453	d='{split:\t:5}'
454	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
455	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
456	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
457	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
458	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
459	fi
460	'''
461	mode = "fork"
462	
463	[actions.copy_resume]
464	description = "Copy 'cd <dir> && <agent> --resume <id>' to clipboard"
465	command = '''
466	agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'
467	case "$agent" in
468	  "[oc]") cmd="opencode --session $sid" ;;
469	  "[cc]") cmd="claude --resume $sid" ;;
470	  "[cx]") cmd="codex resume $sid" ;;
471	  "[cu]") cmd="cursor-agent --resume $sid" ;;
472	  "[ci]") cmd="cursor $dir" ;;
473	esac
474	case "$dir" in
475	  /*) [ "$agent" = "[ci]" ] && line="$cmd" || line=$(printf 'cd %q && %s' "$dir" "$cmd") ;;
476	  *)  line="$cmd" ;;
477	esac
478	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$line" | pbcopy
479	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$line" | wl-copy
480	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$line" | xclip -selection clipboard
481	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$line" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
482	fi
483	'''
484	mode = "fork"
485	
486	[actions.edit_jsonl]
487	description = "Open raw session file in $EDITOR (claude/codex only)"
488	command = '''
489	agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'
490	case "$agent" in
491	  "[cc]") f=$(find "$HOME/.claude/projects" -name "${sid}.jsonl" -not -path "*/subagents/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1) ;;
492	  "[cx]") f=$(find "$HOME/.codex/sessions" -name "rollout-*${sid}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | head -1) ;;
493	  "[oc]") echo "OpenCode sessions live in SQLite — use 'opencode export $sid' instead."; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
494	  "[cu]") echo "Cursor sessions live in opaque BLOBs — no plaintext to edit."; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
495	  "[ci]") echo "Cursor IDE chats live in state.vscdb (cursorDiskKV table) — no plaintext to edit."; echo "Composer ID: $sid"; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
496	esac
497	if [ -z "$f" ] || [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
498	  echo "Session file not found for $sid"; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0
499	fi
500	"${EDITOR:-vi}" "$f"
501	'''
502	mode = "execute"
503
```

```text
1	# 42_gitlab.sh - GitLab helpers using glab CLI (shared bash + zsh).
2	# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/42_gitlab.zsh; the only zsh-ism was
3	# `emulate -L zsh` (gated below).
4	
5	# ==============================================================================
6	# Method 1: Direct shell function (no AI agent needed)
7	# ==============================================================================
8	
9	# Create a GitLab repo under a group from the current git repo, set origin, and push.
10	# Detects current folder name as repo name and current branch automatically.
11	#
12	# Usage:
13	#   glcreate <group> [description]
14	#
15	# Examples:
16	#   glcreate david_quick_tries
17	#   glcreate david_quick_tries "My awesome project"
18	#
19	# If no description is given, the repo is created without one.
20	# The repo is created as private by default.
21	glcreate() {
22	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
23	
24	  local group="${1:?Usage: glcreate <group> [description]}"
25	  local desc="${2:-}"
26	  local name
27	  name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
28	  local branch
29	  branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
30	
31	  echo "Creating: ${group}/${name} (branch: ${branch})"
32	
33	  glab repo create "${group}/${name}" \
34	    --private \
35	    --defaultBranch "$branch" \
36	    --skipGitInit \
37	    ${desc:+--description "$desc"} \
38	  && {
39	    # Add or update origin remote
40	    git remote add origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git" 2>/dev/null \
41	      || git remote set-url origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git"
42	  } \
43	  && git push -u origin "$branch"
44	}
45	
46	# ==============================================================================
47	# Method 2: AI agent assisted (summarizes description from project content)
48	# ==============================================================================
49	
50	# Create a GitLab repo using an AI coding agent to inspect the project,
51	# auto-generate a description, create the repo, set origin, and push.
52	#
53	# Supported agents: opencode (default), claude, codex, cursor-agent
54	# Set GLCREATE_AGENT to change the default agent.
55	# Set GLCREATE_LANG to change the default prompt language (zh or en, default: zh).
56	#
57	# Usage:
58	#   glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent <name>] [--lang zh|en]
59	#
60	# Examples:
61	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries
62	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries "Override description"
63	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --agent claude
64	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --lang en
65	#
66	# If no description is given, the agent will summarize one from the project content.
67	glcreate-ai() {
68	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
69	
70	  local group="" desc="" agent="${GLCREATE_AGENT:-opencode}" lang="${GLCREATE_LANG:-zh}"
71	
72	  # Parse arguments
73	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
74	    case "$1" in
75	      --agent) agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76	      --lang)  lang="$2"; shift 2 ;;
77	      *) [ -z "$group" ] && group="$1" || desc="$1"; shift ;;
78	    esac
79	  done
80	
81	  if [ -z "$group" ]; then
82	    echo "Usage: glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent opencode|claude|codex|cursor-agent] [--lang zh|en]"
83	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_AGENT env var to change default agent (default: opencode)"
84	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_LANG  env var to change default language (default: zh)"
85	    return 1
86	  fi
87	
88	  local name
89	  name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
90	  local branch
91	  branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
92	  local prompt
93	
94	  case "$lang" in
95	    en)
96	      prompt="Use glab to create a private repo under gitlab.com/${group}, repo name: ${name}, default branch: ${branch}. Set the origin remote and push.${desc:+ Description: ${desc}.} If no description is provided, summarize one sentence from the project content."
97	      ;;
98	    zh|*)
99	      prompt="用 glab 把這個 repo 建到 gitlab.com/${group} 底下，repo name: ${name}，private，default branch: ${branch}，設定 origin remote 並 push。${desc:+Description: ${desc}。}如果沒給 description 就根據項目內容總結一句。"
100	      ;;
```

```text
103	  echo "Agent: ${agent} | Lang: ${lang} | Repo: ${group}/${name} | Branch: ${branch}"
104	
105	  case "$agent" in
106	    opencode)       opencode run "$prompt" ;;
107	    claude)         claude -p "$prompt" ;;
108	    codex)          codex exec "$prompt" ;;
109	    cursor-agent)   cursor-agent -p "$prompt" ;;
110	    *)              echo "Unknown agent: ${agent}"; return 1 ;;
111	  esac
112	}
113
```

```text
144	# Invoke a coding-agent in one-shot mode.
145	#
146	# Writes reply (text) to stdout. Writes metadata line to stderr when
147	# AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1 and the agent supports structured JSON output.
148	# Currently only Claude's JSON includes usage/cost — other agents just get a
149	# "<agent> (<model>)" line on stderr.
150	_aiagent_invoke() {
151	  local agent="$1" prompt="$2"
152	  local json reply model_used tokens_in tokens_out cache_read cache_create cost duration rc
153	
154	  # Ensure spinner cleans up if the caller returns or we hit a trap.
155	  trap '_aicap_spinner_stop' EXIT INT TERM
156	
157	  case "$agent" in
158	    claude)
159	      # Conditional --model: empty AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL → claude picks its
160	      # own default (robust if the pinned alias is ever retired).
161	      local -a claude_model_args
162	      claude_model_args=()
163	      [ -n "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL" ] && claude_model_args=(--model "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL")
164	      local claude_model_label="${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL:-(default)}"
165	      if [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" = "1" ] && command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
166	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $claude_model_label (json)…"
167	        json=$(claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" --output-format json "$prompt")
168	        rc=$?
169	        _aicap_spinner_stop
170	        (( rc != 0 )) && return $rc
171	        reply=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.result // empty')
172	        model_used=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.modelUsage | keys | first // "?"')
173	        tokens_in=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.input_tokens // "?"')
174	        tokens_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.output_tokens // "?"')
175	        cache_read=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_read_input_tokens // 0')
176	        cache_create=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens // 0')
177	        cost=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.total_cost_usd // "?"')
178	        duration=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.duration_ms // "?"')
179	        printf '%s\n' "claude ($model_used) | in=$tokens_in out=$tokens_out cache=(r:$cache_read,w:$cache_create) | cost=\$$cost ${duration}ms" >&2
180	        printf '%s\n' "$reply"
181	      else
182	        printf '%s\n' "claude ($claude_model_label)" >&2
183	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $claude_model_label…"
184	        claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
185	        rc=$?
186	        _aicap_spinner_stop
187	        return $rc
188	      fi
189	      ;;
190	    opencode)
191	      local -a opencode_model_args
192	      opencode_model_args=()
193	      [ -n "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL" ] && opencode_model_args=(-m "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL")
194	      local opencode_model_label="${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL:-(default)}"
195	      printf '%s\n' "opencode ($opencode_model_label)" >&2
196	      _aicap_spinner_start "opencode $opencode_model_label…"
197	      opencode run "${opencode_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
198	      rc=$?
199	      _aicap_spinner_stop
200	      return $rc
201	      ;;
202	    codex)
203	      # AICAP_CODEX_MODEL defaults to empty since gpt-5-mini is rejected on
204	      # ChatGPT-account auth. Users on API-key auth can re-pin via the env.
205	      local -a codex_model_args
206	      codex_model_args=()
207	      [ -n "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL" ] && codex_model_args=(-m "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL")
208	      local codex_model_label="${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL:-(default)}"
209	      printf '%s\n' "codex ($codex_model_label)" >&2
210	      _aicap_spinner_start "codex $codex_model_label…"
211	      codex exec "${codex_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
212	      rc=$?
213	      _aicap_spinner_stop
214	      return $rc
215	      ;;
216	    cursor-agent)
217	      if [ -n "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" ]; then
218	        printf '%s\n' "cursor-agent ($AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL)" >&2
219	        _aicap_spinner_start "cursor-agent $AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL…"
220	        cursor-agent -p --model "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" "$prompt"
221	      else
222	        printf '%s\n' "cursor-agent" >&2
223	        _aicap_spinner_start "cursor-agent…"
224	        cursor-agent -p "$prompt"
225	      fi
226	      rc=$?
227	      _aicap_spinner_stop
228	      return $rc
229	      ;;
230	    http)
231	      # OpenAI-compatible chat-completions over curl. Covers OpenRouter (with
232	      # API key) and local Ollama (no auth) with the same code path. Never
233	      # auto-detected — opt in via AICAP_AGENT=http or `-a http`.
234	      local url="$AICAP_HTTP_URL" model="$AICAP_HTTP_MODEL"
235	      local key="${AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:-${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}}"
236	      if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
237	        printf '%s\n' "aifix: jq is required for the http agent" >&2
238	        return 1
239	      fi
240	      if ! command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
241	        printf '%s\n' "aifix: curl is required for the http agent" >&2
242	        return 1
243	      fi
244	      # Extract host from URL. Original used zsh-nested `${${url#*://}%%/*}`;
245	      # bash doesn't support nested expansion, so do it in two steps.
246	      local host
247	      host="${url#*://}"
248	      host="${host%%/*}"
249	      [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" != "1" ] && printf '%s\n' "http ($model @ $host)" >&2
250	      _aicap_spinner_start "http $model…"
251	      local payload response
252	      payload=$(jq -n --arg m "$model" --arg p "$prompt" \
253	        '{model: $m, messages: [{role: "user", content: $p}], stream: false}')
254	      local -a curl_args
255	      curl_args=(-sS -X POST "$url" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$payload")
256	      [ -n "$key" ] && curl_args+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $key")
257	      response=$(curl "${curl_args[@]}")
258	      rc=$?
259	      _aicap_spinner_stop
260	      if (( rc != 0 )); then
261	        printf '%s\n' "http: curl failed (rc=$rc) — check AICAP_HTTP_URL ($url)" >&2
262	        return $rc
263	      fi
264	      local err
265	      err=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.error.message // (.error | strings) // empty' 2>/dev/null)
266	      if [ -n "$err" ]; then
267	        printf '%s\n' "http: API error: $err" >&2
268	        return 1
269	      fi
270	      reply=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.choices[0].message.content // empty')
271	      if [ -z "$reply" ]; then
272	        printf '%s\n' "http: empty reply (raw response: $response)" >&2
273	        return 1
274	      fi
275	      if [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" = "1" ]; then
276	        tokens_in=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.usage.prompt_tokens // "?"')
277	        tokens_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.usage.completion_tokens // "?"')
278	        printf '%s\n' "http ($model @ $host) | in=$tokens_in out=$tokens_out" >&2
279	      fi
280	      printf '%s\n' "$reply"
281	      ;;
282	    *) printf '%s\n' "aifix: unknown agent '$agent' (supported: opencode, claude, codex, cursor-agent, http)" >&2; return 1 ;;
283	  esac
```

- **Continue**: `-c` / `--continue` (most recent), `-r` / `--resume [id]` (by id/picker)

# Plan: Quick "run a prompt through coding agent X" shell wrappers

## Context

The repo already has rich AI capture tooling (`aifix`, `aiexplain`, `aiblock`,
`aifix-run`, `aifix-rerun`) in `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh`, but those
are all **single-turn diagnose-the-output** wrappers — they require a captured
terminal block, stdin, a tee'd command, or shell-history rerun. None of them
let you just type a fresh prompt and stream the agent's reply back.

The user wants short mnemonics that mirror the agent-session tags in
`dot_config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml:17-19` (`[oc]`/`[cc]`/`[cx]`/`[cu]`):

- `ocr "prompt"` → `opencode run …`
- `ccr "prompt"` → `claude -p …`
- `cxr "prompt"` → `codex exec …`
- `cur "prompt"` → `cursor-agent -p …`
- `olr "prompt"` → `ollama run …` (sugar over local Ollama)
- `air "prompt"` → autodetect via `AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY`, supports `-a` / `-m`

These pair the "browse sessions" UX (`tv agent-sessions`) with a matching
"start a new one-shot" UX. No naming collisions in `docs/shells/aliases.md`
(`ocr`/`ccr`/`cxr`/`cur`/`olr`/`air` are all free; `cur` ≠ `curl` by length;
`ocr` doesn't shadow any installed binary on either reference machine).

The existing `_aiagent_invoke` helper in `04_ai_capture.sh:150-284`
**should not be reused** for this — when `AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1` the Claude
branch (lines 167-180) forces full-buffer capture of the reply via
`json=$(claude -p … --output-format json …)` so it can parse usage/cost
out of the JSON. That kills streaming for long agent responses. The clean
precedent is `glcreate-ai` in `dot_config/shell/42_gitlab.sh:105-111`,
which inlines the per-agent CLI dispatch directly and streams stdout.

---

## Implementation

### 1. New file: `dot_config/shell/05_ai_run.sh` (~140 lines)

POSIX-compatible shared file (both shells source it via the standard
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell/*.sh` loader). Number `05` deliberately places it
**after** `04_ai_agents.sh` (SSOT) and `04_ai_capture.sh` so it can:
- Inherit `AICAP_*_MODEL` env vars
- Reuse `_aiagent_autodetect` from `04_ai_capture.sh:77-94` for `air`

**Header comment** must explain the deliberate diverge from `aifix`:
- These wrappers stream stdout straight through (no spinner, no metadata).
- They are pass-through: extra flags forward to the underlying CLI, so
  `ccr -c "prompt"` → `claude -p --model haiku -c "prompt"` (continue last
  session). Same for `--resume`, custom `--model` overrides, etc.
- Ollama is intentionally NOT added to `_aiagent_invoke` or the autodetect
  priority — `olr` is a shell-only sugar wrapper; the four Python
  consumers of the SSOT (per the CLAUDE.md cross-file rule) do not need
  to know about it. The existing `http` agent path remains the
  cross-platform OpenAI-compat fallback (covers OpenRouter + remote
  endpoints + Ollama-via-localhost when the user prefers that).

**Per-agent wrappers (5 functions):** each ~10 lines, identical shape —
empty-arg → usage; build conditional model-args array; exec CLI with
`"$@"` pass-through. Model-args array is empty when the SSOT pin is
empty, so the CLI's own default applies (matches the
`AICAP_<AGENT>_MODEL`-conditional pattern at `04_ai_capture.sh:161-163`,
`192-193`, `206-207`, `216-220`).

\```sh
ocr() {                                      # opencode → [oc]
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && { printf '%s\n' "usage: ocr [opencode flags] <prompt>" >&2; return 1; }
  local -a model_args=()
  [ -n "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL" ] && model_args=(-m "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL")
  opencode run "${model_args[@]}" "$@"
}

ccr() {                                      # claude → [cc]
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && { printf '%s\n' "usage: ccr [claude flags] <prompt>" >&2; return 1; }
  local -a model_args=()
  [ -n "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL" ] && model_args=(--model "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL")
  claude -p "${model_args[@]}" "$@"
}

cxr() {                                      # codex → [cx]
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && { printf '%s\n' "usage: cxr [codex flags] <prompt>" >&2; return 1; }
  local -a model_args=()
  [ -n "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL" ] && model_args=(-m "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL")
  codex exec "${model_args[@]}" "$@"
}

cur() {                                      # cursor-agent → [cu]
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && { printf '%s\n' "usage: cur [cursor-agent flags] <prompt>" >&2; return 1; }
  local -a model_args=()
  [ -n "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" ] && model_args=(--model "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL")
  cursor-agent -p "${model_args[@]}" "$@"
}

olr() {                                      # ollama (shell-only sugar)
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && { printf '%s\n' "usage: olr <prompt>   (model = \$AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL)" >&2; return 1; }
  local model="${AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL:-qwen2.5-coder:7b}"
  ollama run "$model" "$@"
}
\```

Note `olr` is **prompt-only** (no pass-through) because `ollama run` puts
the model positionally before the prompt — mixing flags in `"$@"` would
land them after the model and break parsing. Documented in the header.
For advanced ollama use, drop to `ollama run` directly or set
`AICAP_AGENT=http air "…"` for the OpenAI-compat path.

**Autodetect wrapper `air`** (~40 lines): parses `-a AGENT`, `-m MODEL`,
`-h|--help`, `--` separator, then dispatches to one of the five wrappers
above. Subshell isolation for the `-m` override so per-call model
selection doesn't leak into the parent shell:

\```sh
air() {
  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
  local agent="" model_override=""
  local -a prompt_args=()
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      -a|--agent) agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
      -m|--model) model_override="$2"; shift 2 ;;
      -h|--help)
        printf '%s\n' \
          "usage: air [-a AGENT] [-m MODEL] [--] <prompt> [flags…]" \
          "  -a AGENT   opencode | claude | codex | cursor-agent | ollama | http" \
          "             (default: \$AICAP_AGENT or auto-detect via \$AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY)" \
          "  -m MODEL   override the agent's AICAP_<AGENT>_MODEL pin for this call" \
          "  --         end of air flags; everything after is forwarded to the agent CLI"
        return 0 ;;
      --) shift; prompt_args+=("$@"); break ;;
      *)  prompt_args+=("$1"); shift ;;
    esac
  done
  [ "${#prompt_args[@]}" -eq 0 ] && { printf '%s\n' "air: missing prompt (try: air -h)" >&2; return 1; }

  if [ -z "$agent" ]; then
    agent="${AICAP_AGENT:-$(_aiagent_autodetect)}" || {
      printf '%s\n' "air: no agent CLI on PATH (priority: \$AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY)" >&2
      printf '%s\n' "air: hint — AICAP_AGENT=http air … for OpenRouter/Ollama HTTP" >&2
      return 1
    }
  fi

  case "$agent" in
    opencode|oc)     ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL="$model_override"; ocr "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    claude|cc)       ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL="$model_override";   ccr "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    codex|cx)        ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_CODEX_MODEL="$model_override";    cxr "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    cursor-agent|cu) ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL="$model_override";   cur "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    ollama|ol)       ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL="$model_override";   olr "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    http)            ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_HTTP_MODEL="$model_override"
                       # `_aiagent_invoke` is fine here because http isn't streaming-sensitive
                       # (curl returns the full JSON response in one go anyway).
                       _aiagent_invoke http "${prompt_args[*]}" ) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' "air: unknown agent '$agent' (supported: opencode, claude, codex, cursor-agent, ollama, http)" >&2; return 1 ;;
  esac
}
\```

### 2. Edit: `dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh` (SSOT) — add one line

Add `AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL` to the env-var block near the other
`AICAP_*_MODEL` lines. Default to `qwen2.5-coder:7b` (a sensible Ollama
coding model). Export at the bottom alongside the others.

\```sh
: "${AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL:=qwen2.5-coder:7b}"
…
export AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL
\```

This is the **only** SSOT change. We deliberately do NOT add `ollama` to
`AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY` (parallels how `http` is opt-in per the comment at
`04_ai_capture.sh:42`).

### 3. Edit: `docs/shells/aliases.md` — add rows in the AI Capture section

Add 6 rows mirroring the existing aifix/aiexplain entries (function,
source file, scope, one-line). Reference `04_ai_run.sh` as the source.
Add a short note that these are streaming pass-through wrappers (unlike
aifix which is capture-and-diagnose).

### 4. NOT changed: CLAUDE.md cross-file rule for the AICAP SSOT

The existing rule covers "when adding a NEW agent" — ollama is not being
added as a new AICAP agent in the canonical sense (it's not in
`_aiagent_invoke`, not in autodetect, not parsed by the four Python
consumers). The shell-only `olr` wrapper and the new
`AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL` env var are documented in the new file's header
comment, which is sufficient.

7. **No-arg usage**: each of `ocr` / `ccr` / `cxr` / `cur` / `olr` / `air`
   with zero args should print a usage line to stderr and exit 1.
8. **Bash compatibility**: `bash -c 'source ~/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh; source ~/.config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh; source ~/.config/shell/05_ai_run.sh; type air'`

```sh
# 05_ai_run.sh — quick "run one prompt through coding agent X" wrappers
#
#   ocr "prompt"      → opencode run     (agent tag [oc])
#   ccr "prompt"      → claude -p        (agent tag [cc])
#   cxr "prompt"      → codex exec       (agent tag [cx])
#   cur "prompt"      → cursor-agent -p  (agent tag [cu])
#   olr "prompt"      → ollama run       (shell-only sugar — see note below)
#   air "prompt"      → autodetect via $AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY, -a / -m overrides
#
# Mnemonic mirrors the agent-session tags in
# dot_config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml so muscle memory
# carries across `tv agent-sessions` (browse old) and these (start new).
#
# Difference from aifix / aiexplain (dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh):
#   - aifix is capture-and-diagnose: needs a captured terminal block,
#     stdin, a tee'd run, or shell-history rerun.
#   - These wrappers just forward a fresh prompt and stream the agent's
#     reply straight back. No spinner, no metadata, no buffering.
#
# Pass-through forwarding: extra flags reach the underlying CLI, so
#   ccr -c 'continue from prior turn'
# expands to `claude -p --model haiku -c 'continue from prior turn'`
# (continue last session). Same trick works for `--resume`, custom
# `--model` overrides (claude honors the last `--model` flag), etc.
# Exception: `olr` is prompt-only, see comment on the function.
#
# Ollama note: `olr` is intentionally **not** an AICAP agent in the
# canonical sense — it does not appear in `_aiagent_invoke`, is not in
# the autodetect priority, and the four Python consumers of the SSOT
# (per the CLAUDE.md cross-file rule) do not parse `AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL`.
# `olr` is shell-only sugar over `ollama run`. The cross-platform
# OpenRouter / OpenAI-compat / remote-Ollama-via-HTTP path is the
# existing `http` agent in 04_ai_capture.sh — opt in via
# `AICAP_AGENT=http air "…"`.

# Defensive load: if 04_ai_agents.sh wasn't sourced first, pull it in.
# Same pattern as 04_ai_capture.sh.
if [ -z "${_AICAP_AGENT_CONFIG_SOURCED:-}" ] && [ -r "$HOME/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$HOME/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh"
fi

ocr() {
  if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "usage: ocr [opencode flags] <prompt>" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  local -a model_args=()
  [ -n "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL" ] && model_args=(-m "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL")
  opencode run "${model_args[@]}" "$@"
}

ccr() {
  if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "usage: ccr [claude flags] <prompt>" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  local -a model_args=()
  [ -n "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL" ] && model_args=(--model "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL")
  claude -p "${model_args[@]}" "$@"
}

cxr() {
  if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "usage: cxr [codex flags] <prompt>" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  local -a model_args=()
  [ -n "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL" ] && model_args=(-m "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL")
  codex exec "${model_args[@]}" "$@"
}

cur() {
  if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "usage: cur [cursor-agent flags] <prompt>" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  local -a model_args=()
  [ -n "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" ] && model_args=(--model "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL")
  cursor-agent -p "${model_args[@]}" "$@"
}

# `ollama run MODEL [PROMPT]` puts the model positionally before the
# prompt, so pass-through would land user flags AFTER the model and
# break parsing. Treat "$@" as the prompt only. Advanced ollama flags
# → drop to `ollama run` directly, or use `air -a http` for the
# OpenAI-compat path against localhost:11434.
olr() {
  if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "usage: olr <prompt>   (model = \$AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL = ${AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL:-<unset>})" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  local model="${AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL:-qwen2.5-coder:7b}"
  ollama run "$model" "$@"
}

air() {
  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
  local agent="" model_override=""
  local -a prompt_args=()
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      -a|--agent) agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
      -m|--model) model_override="$2"; shift 2 ;;
      -h|--help)
        printf '%s\n' \
          "usage: air [-a AGENT] [-m MODEL] [--] <prompt> [agent flags…]" \
          "" \
          "  -a AGENT   opencode | claude | codex | cursor-agent | ollama | http" \
          "             (default: \$AICAP_AGENT, else auto-detect via \$AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY)" \
          "  -m MODEL   override AICAP_<AGENT>_MODEL for this call only" \
          "  --         end of air flags; everything after forwards to the agent CLI" \
          "" \
          "env (current):" \
          "  AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY = ${AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY}" \
          "  AICAP_AGENT          = ${AICAP_AGENT:-<unset = auto-detect>}" \
          "  AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL:-<unset>}" \
          "  AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL = ${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL:-<unset>}" \
          "  AICAP_CODEX_MODEL    = ${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL:-<unset>}" \
          "  AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL:-<unset>}" \
          "  AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL   = ${AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL:-<unset>}" \
          "  AICAP_HTTP_MODEL     = ${AICAP_HTTP_MODEL:-<unset>}"
        return 0 ;;
      --) shift; prompt_args+=("$@"); break ;;
      -*) prompt_args+=("$1"); shift ;;
      *)  prompt_args+=("$1"); shift ;;
    esac
  done
  if [ "${#prompt_args[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "air: missing prompt (try: air -h)" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if [ -z "$agent" ]; then
    if [ -n "${AICAP_AGENT:-}" ]; then
      agent="$AICAP_AGENT"
    else
      agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
        printf '%s\n' "air: no agent CLI on PATH (priority: \$AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY = $AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY)" >&2
        printf '%s\n' "air: hint — set AICAP_AGENT=http or pass -a http for OpenRouter/Ollama HTTP" >&2
        return 1
      }
    fi
  fi

  # Subshell isolates the per-call -m override so it doesn't leak.
  case "$agent" in
    opencode|oc)     ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL="$model_override"; ocr "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    claude|cc)       ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL="$model_override";   ccr "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    codex|cx)        ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_CODEX_MODEL="$model_override";    cxr "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    cursor-agent|cu) ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL="$model_override";   cur "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    ollama|ol)       ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_OLLAMA_MODEL="$model_override";   olr "${prompt_args[@]}" ) ;;
    http)
      # `_aiagent_invoke` is fine here: curl returns the full JSON in one
      # shot anyway, so streaming isn't a factor. Joining prompt_args
      # with single spaces matches how 04_ai_capture.sh constructs the
      # http payload (single text content string).
      ( [ -n "$model_override" ] && AICAP_HTTP_MODEL="$model_override"
        _aiagent_invoke http "${prompt_args[*]}" )
      ;;
    *)
      printf '%s\n' "air: unknown agent '$agent' (supported: opencode|oc, claude|cc, codex|cx, cursor-agent|cu, ollama|ol, http)" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

```

## Summary

Implemented per the approved plan:

- **`dot_config/shell/05_ai_run.sh`** (new) — 6 functions: `ocr` / `ccr` / `cxr` / `cur` / `olr` / `air`. Streaming pass-through (no spinner/metadata buffering, unlike `aifix`), flag forwarding for the four pro-CLIs, subshell-isolated `-m`/`-a` per-call overrides for `air`.

Verified: both shells parse the file; all 6 functions register; no-arg paths exit 1 with usage; `air -h` prints env snapshot; live smoke `ccr "…"` returned `pong` and `air -a claude "…"` returned `ack`.

## On shellcheck

Worth adding — there are 45+ `.sh`/`.zsh`/`.bash` files in this repo and the only current "validation" is "run it and hope". Lightweight (single static binary, ~few MB), well-maintained, and would catch the kind of POSIX-vs-bash drift the three-tier rule cares about (`dot_config/shell/` must source clean in both shells). Tradeoff: it pulls in one more devtools dep and you'd want to either run it gated by `command -v shellcheck` in CI or accept a few hundred existing warnings on the first pass.

Want me to:
1. Add it to `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` only (passive install, no enforcement), or
2. Also add a `just lint-shell` recipe + a pre-commit hook that runs it on changed `.sh`/`.bash` files?

(1) is the minimal "have the tool around" version; (2) is the "actually enforce it" version which means cleaning up the existing-warnings backlog first.
